intro: Hi! In this lesson you'll learn have and have got, the words for 'punya': I have two sisters, She's got long hair. You'll talk about your family, your things and what people look like, and make negatives and questions. Warm-up: how many brothers and sisters do you have?
teachingNotes: 'Have' = punya. With he, she, it the form is **has**: *She has two sisters*. The #1 error is *'She have'* (Indonesian 'punya' never changes).

Say why: most verbs just add -s with he/she/it (work → works), but have is an exception: it becomes has, never 'haves'. After does/doesn't the verb goes back to its basic form (doesn't have, Does she have), because does already shows he/she. Explain 'subject' plainly (who has it), and the apostrophe in I've / she's (letters left out).

'Have got' means the same as 'have' for possessions, family and appearance (common in British English). Contractions: I've got, she's got. Before 'got', 's = has, not is (*She's got* = She has got). Do not use 'have got' for actions like *have breakfast* or *have a shower*.

Two systems, never mixed. have: don't/doesn't have, Do/Does ... have? (Yes, I do.). have got: haven't/hasn't got, Have/Has ... got? (Yes, I have.). Common errors: *'Do you have got a pen?'*, *'She doesn't has'*, *'I haven't a car'* (say I don't have a car / I haven't got a car).

Things that look like exceptions, explain them: hair (one mass, no -s) vs eyes (two separate things, -s); child → children (special plural); have breakfast / have a shower = an action, not 'punya'; sister/brother = kakak or adik. Spelling: grey and moustache are British; American English writes gray and mustache. Have got is mainly British; Americans mostly say have.

Appearance: Indonesian 'Rambutnya panjang' leads to *'She is long hair'*. Teach *She has long hair* or *Her hair is long*. 'Hair' is uncountable here (long hair, not long hairs), and adjectives go before the noun, length before colour (long black hair).

Limits: only the present. Don't teach 'had', 'has got' as a present perfect, or 'there is/are'. Keep sentences short with family, things and appearance vocabulary (sister, son, motorbike, laptop, hair, eyes, beard, moustache).

keyPoints.title: have / has for family and things
keyPoints.explanation: Use have (= punya) for family and things you own. I, you, we, they have; he, she, it has. Most verbs just add -s with he/she/it (work → works), but have is special: it becomes has. Never 'she have' or 'he haves'.

id.title: have / has untuk keluarga dan barang
id.explanation: Pakai have (= punya) untuk keluarga dan barang yang kamu miliki. I, you, we, they pakai have; he, she, it pakai has. Kebanyakan kata kerja cukup ditambah -s untuk he/she/it (work → works), tapi have itu khusus: berubah jadi has. Jangan pernah 'she have' atau 'he haves'.

keyPoints.title: Describing appearance with have
keyPoints.explanation: Use have/has (got) + adjective + noun for hair, eyes, a beard or a moustache: She has long hair. Not 'She is long hair'. You can also say: Her hair is long. Hair has no -s (it's one mass), but eyes has -s (two separate eyes).

examples.en: My father has got a moustache.

id.title: Menggambarkan penampilan dengan have
id.explanation: Pakai have/has (got) + kata sifat + kata benda untuk rambut, mata, jenggot atau kumis: She has long hair. Bukan 'She is long hair'. Kamu juga bisa bilang: Her hair is long. Hair tidak diberi -s (dianggap satu kesatuan), tapi eyes diberi -s (dua mata yang terpisah).

keyPoints.title: Negatives and questions: two systems
keyPoints.explanation: With have: I don't have / she doesn't have; Do you have ...? — Yes, I do. After does/doesn't, has goes back to have, because does already shows he/she. With have got: I haven't got / she hasn't got; Have you got ...? — Yes, I have. Don't mix them: never 'Do you have got ...?'.

examples.en: I don't have a laptop. = I haven't got a laptop.
Do you have a pen? — Yes, I do.
Has she got a sister? — No, she hasn't.

id.title: Kalimat negatif dan pertanyaan: dua cara
id.explanation: Dengan have: I don't have / she doesn't have; Do you have ...? — Yes, I do. Setelah does/doesn't, has kembali jadi have, karena does sudah menunjukkan he/she. Dengan have got: I haven't got / she hasn't got; Have you got ...? — Yes, I have. Jangan dicampur: jangan pernah 'Do you have got ...?'.

assessment.prompt: Choose the correct answer. Complete with have or has: Pak Joko and his wife ___ two daughters.
assessment.rubric: Correct: have (Pak Joko and his wife = they). 'has' = 0 (the subject is two people). 'are have' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Choose the correct answer. Listen to Dewi. How many brothers has she got? Choose the number.
assessment.listen: Hi, I'm Dewi. I've got two brothers and one sister.
assessment.rubric: Correct: two (2). 'one' or 'three' = 0 (one is the number of sisters; three is all her brothers and sisters).

assessment.prompt: Choose the correct answer. Translate into English: Dia (perempuan) punya mata cokelat.
assessment.rubric: Correct: She has brown eyes / She's got brown eyes. 'She have brown eyes' = 50. 'She is brown eyes' = 20. 'He has ...' = 50. 'eyes brown' (wrong order) = 50.

assessment.prompt: Choose the correct answer. Correct the mistake: My brother is short hair.
assessment.rubric: Correct: My brother has short hair (or has got / 's got). 'My brother have short hair' = 50. 'short hairs' = 70.

assessment.prompt: Choose the correct answer. Make it negative with doesn't: Rina has a car.
assessment.rubric: Correct: Rina doesn't have a car. 'Rina doesn't has a car' = 50. 'Rina hasn't got a car' = 70 (correct English, but the task asks for doesn't). 'Rina hasn't a car' = 30.

assessment.prompt: Choose the correct answer. Make a question: They've got a big house.
assessment.rubric: Correct: Have they got a big house? 'Do they have a big house?' = 80 (correct, but it drops got). 'Do they have got a big house?' = 30. 'They have got a big house?' (statement order) = 30.
options: Have they got a big house
Have got they a big house?
Has they got a big house?
assessment.correctOption: Have they got a big house

assessment.prompt: Choose the correct answer. Give a short negative answer: Has your brother got a bicycle?
assessment.rubric: Correct: No, he hasn't. 'No, he doesn't' = 50 (the question uses has ... got, so answer with hasn't). 'No, he isn't' = 20. 'No' alone = 30.

blocks.text: **have** means *punya*. Use it for your **family** and the **things you own**. With I, you, we, they say **have**. With he, she, it say **has**: *I have a sister. My sister has a son.* Why not *haves*? Most verbs just add -s with he/she/it (*work → works*), but **have** is an exception: it changes to **has**. You just have to remember this one.

id.text: **have** artinya *punya*. Pakai untuk **keluarga** dan **barang milikmu**. Dengan I, you, we, they pakai **have**. Dengan he, she, it pakai **has**: *I have a sister. My sister has a son.* Kenapa bukan *haves*? Kebanyakan kata kerja cukup ditambah -s untuk he/she/it (*work → works*), tapi **have** adalah pengecualian: berubah jadi **has**. Yang satu ini cukup dihafal.

rows.id: Saya punya dua saudara perempuan. (*sister* = kakak atau adik perempuan)

rows.en: My parents have a warung in Bandung.
rows.id: Orang tua saya punya warung di Bandung.
Sari punya tiga anak. (*child* = satu anak, *children* = beberapa anak: bentuk khusus, tanpa -s)

blocks.text: In Indonesian, *punya* never changes. In English, check the **subject** (who has it): one person or thing (he, she, it, Sari, my father) → **has**.

id.text: Dalam bahasa Indonesia, *punya* tidak pernah berubah. Dalam bahasa Inggris, cek **subjeknya** (siapa yang punya): satu orang atau benda (he, she, it, Sari, my father) → **has**.

blocks.prompt: My uncle ___ a shop in Medan.
blocks.explain: My uncle = he, so use has. Don't put is before have: 'punya' is just have/has, with no am/is/are.

id.explain: My uncle = he, jadi pakai has. Jangan taruh is sebelum have: 'punya' cukup have/has, tanpa am/is/are.
id.prompt: Lengkapi: My uncle ___ a shop in Medan.

blocks.text: **have got** means the same as **have** when we talk about family, things and appearance. It is very common in British English (Americans mostly just say *have*) and usually short: **I've got** = I have got, **she's got** = she has got. The mark **'** shows that letters are left out. Before *got*, **'s = has**, not *is*. If a describing word or an -ing word comes next (*she's tired*), 's = is.

id.text: **have got** artinya sama dengan **have** saat membicarakan keluarga, barang dan ciri fisik. Bentuk ini sangat umum di bahasa Inggris Britania (orang Amerika lebih sering bilang *have* saja) dan biasanya disingkat: **I've got** = I have got, **she's got** = she has got. Tanda **'** menunjukkan ada huruf yang dihilangkan. Sebelum *got*, **'s = has**, bukan *is*. Kalau sesudahnya kata sifat atau kata -ing (*she's tired*), 's = is.

id.note: artinya sama dengan I have two brothers.

blocks.text: Use only **have** (not *have got*) for actions: *I have breakfast at six*, not *I've got breakfast at six*. Here **have** doesn't mean *punya*: *have breakfast* = sarapan, *have a shower* = mandi, *have lunch* = makan siang.

id.text: Untuk kegiatan, pakai **have** saja (bukan *have got*): *I have breakfast at six*, bukan *I've got breakfast at six*. Di sini **have** tidak berarti *punya*: *have breakfast* = sarapan, *have a shower* = mandi, *have lunch* = makan siang.

blocks.text: To describe a person, use **have/has (got)** + adjective + noun: *She has long hair. He's got a beard.* Put the adjective **before** the noun: length, then colour: *long black hair*. **Hair** has no -s: *long hair*, not *long hairs*. Why, when **eyes** has -s? The hair on your head is seen as one whole thing (like *rambut*), but eyes are two separate things you can count.

id.text: Untuk mendeskripsikan orang, pakai **have/has (got)** + kata sifat + kata benda: *She has long hair. He's got a beard.* Kata sifat ada **sebelum** kata benda: panjang-pendek dulu, lalu warna: *long black hair*. **Hair** tanpa -s: *long hair*, bukan *long hairs*. Kenapa, padahal **eyes** pakai -s? Rambut di kepala dianggap satu kesatuan (seperti *rambut*), sedangkan mata adalah dua benda terpisah yang bisa dihitung.

rows.en: My father has got a moustache.

rows.id: Nenek rambutnya beruban. (*Grandma's* di sini = Grandma has, karena sesudahnya *got*)

blocks.text: Indonesian says *Rambutnya panjang*. In English don't say *She is long hair*. Say **She has long hair** or **Her hair is long**.

id.text: Bahasa Indonesia bilang *Rambutnya panjang*. Dalam bahasa Inggris jangan bilang *She is long hair*. Katakan **She has long hair** atau **Her hair is long**.

blocks.text: Spelling: **grey** and **moustache** are British. In American English you'll see **gray** and **mustache**. Both are correct; they mean the same.

id.text: Ejaan: **grey** dan **moustache** adalah ejaan Britania. Di bahasa Inggris Amerika kamu akan melihat **gray** dan **mustache**. Dua-duanya benar dan artinya sama.

blocks.explain: Andi = he, so use has. Use have/has, not is, for a beard, hair or eyes.

id.explain: Andi = he, jadi pakai has. Untuk jenggot, rambut atau mata pakai have/has, bukan is.

blocks.text: There are **two systems**. Choose one and don't mix them. **have** works like other verbs: *I don't have*, *she doesn't have*, *Do you have ...? — Yes, I do.* After **does/doesn't**, *has* goes back to **have**, because *does* already shows he/she. **have got** uses have/has itself: *I haven't got*, *she hasn't got*, *Have you got ...? — Yes, I have.*

id.text: Ada **dua sistem**. Pilih salah satu dan jangan dicampur. **have** seperti kata kerja lain: *I don't have*, *she doesn't have*, *Do you have ...? — Yes, I do.* Setelah **does/doesn't**, *has* kembali jadi **have**, karena *does* sudah menunjukkan he/she. **have got** memakai have/has itu sendiri: *I haven't got*, *she hasn't got*, *Have you got ...? — Yes, I have.*

id.note: artinya sama dengan I haven't got a laptop.
artinya sama dengan Dimas hasn't got a sister.

rows.en: Do you have a pen? — Yes, I do.
Has she got a sister? — No, she hasn't.

blocks.text: Three mistakes to avoid: *Do you have got a pen?* (say Do you have / Have you got), *She doesn't has* (say doesn't have: only one -s, and *does* has it) and *I haven't a car* (old-fashioned; say I don't have / I haven't got a car).

id.text: Tiga kesalahan yang harus dihindari: *Do you have got a pen?* (katakan Do you have / Have you got), *She doesn't has* (katakan doesn't have: -s cukup satu, dan sudah ada di *does*) dan *I haven't a car* (kuno; katakan I don't have / I haven't got a car).

blocks.prompt: Does your sister have a laptop? — Yes, she ___.
blocks.explain: The question starts with Does, so the short answer uses does: Yes, she does.

id.explain: Pertanyaannya diawali Does, jadi jawaban singkatnya memakai does: Yes, she does.
